top_rigor_problems: Biography and fact slips under narrative compression: #20 puts Martin's baptism after his discharge (the record has baptism at twenty, then two more years in the army); #10 says Salvian has no monastic tie, though the source record calls him a Lerins-circle associate of Honoratus.

Confident 'No' where the records are silent or the frame is wrong: #8 denies inherited guilt outright though voice_craft declined F1-T-01 for lack of any record; #7 recasts Egypt's novice at the door as 'an unbeliever'.

Smaller precision drifts: Egypt credited with the Palestinian day hours (#21), Vincent's test called 'never consistently applied' when the record keeps that contested (#6), and Vincent's anathema left out of the outsiders answer (#28).
top_access_problems: Length and repetition: the same set pieces (devil in purple, half-cloak, elder breaking his fast, 'not I but the grace of God', Cassian's 'not even a year') recur across #1-4, #7, #15, #17, #27, often padding answers past 400 words.

Build and system language reaching participants: 'tags', 'this record does not hold' (#10), 'the ground given for this turn' (#26), and 'the one private word ... we hold' / 'any record we hold' (#1-3, #15).
Engine-cut orphans and long quotations: a dangling 'He' in #18 and #22, a 300-word quote with a 68-word sentence in #18, and a 90-word quote in #3.
world_summary.cost_note: Output averaged roughly 700 tokens. Answers longer than their value: #10 (675 words, about 420 beyond need), #18 (633, about 300, mostly the quotation), #15 (548, about 280), #7 (497, about 250), #2 (459, about 220), #4 (424, about 200) and #3 (394, about 160). Capping answers near 280 words and banning repeated set-piece exempla would cut output tokens by roughly a third with no loss of substance. #24, #25 and #20 show the right size.
world_summary.go_live_view: Close but not yet. 16 of 28 answers ship as they are, and 8 more are sound but need craft fixes, and the world's honest-limit discipline is a real strength: the Tours/Marseilles split, Egypt named as the source, the island's silence and the missing women's voices all come through well, as #22, #24 and #25 show. Four answers carry errors a historian would catch (#20 baptism order, #10 Salvian, #8 an unsupported 'No' on original sin, #7 'unbeliever' at the monastery door). Several more leak build vocabulary or engine cuts. The single most valuable fix is a length-and-reuse discipline in the voice: one exemplum per answer, no set-piece repeated from the stock (cloak, devil in purple, guest-elder), and a ceiling near 280 words. That would remove most of the padding and the orphaned-pronoun cuts, and a short rule against flat denials where voice_craft has declined a cell would catch #8.
